summary: Federal election day is fixed by law as the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even years.
realLife: Federal law sets the day for electing Representatives and Delegates to Congress as the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November, in every even-numbered year.
sources: Cornell Legal Information Institute, 2 U.S. Code Section 7, Time of election: https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/2/7
inGame: the elections module's calendar rows, read by the loading screen's progress step for elections (loading-steps.elections).

turns.what: A state moves its own offices to a different date.
turns.pulledBy: a state law on its election calendar
turns.writesBack: an election row on another day than the federal one

turns.what: A runoff or special election lands on a different day for one seat.
turns.pulledBy: a vacancy or a runoff rule
turns.writesBack: an extra election row for that seat
